# Benchmark 02: Academic Literature Review

* **Domain:** Computer Science / Distributed Systems  
* **Target Persona:** Academic / Scholarly (Relational Synthesis)

---

## 1. Raw AI Input (Generated by Baseline LLM)

> Distributed consensus algorithms play a pivotal role in modern computer science. Over the years, numerous researchers have delved into the intricacies of Paxos and Raft. It is important to note that Paxos provides robust theoretical guarantees for fault tolerance (Lamport, 1998). Moreover, Raft offers an understandable alternative without sacrificing safety (Ongaro and Ousterhout, 2014). In summary, both algorithms serve as a beacon of innovation in distributed systems, unlocking powerful consensus capabilities across cloud clusters.

## 3. Humanized Prose Output (`rewriter_agent` after Quality Gate Approval)

> Lamport (1998) established the theoretical foundation of fault-tolerant state machines with Paxos, but its non-intuitive leader-election protocol created notorious implementation hurdles in production clusters. To address this comprehensibility gap, Ongaro and Ousterhout (2014) restructured consensus around explicit leader terms in Raft. The trade-off is architectural rather than theoretical: Raft trades Paxos's symmetric state machine flexibility for decomposed RPC invariants that developers can actually debug.
